14:38 Local Time, 05:08 GMT, 10:38 IST: Bangladesh have pulled off the unthinkable! They have humbled the No. 1 Test playing nation in their own backyard! This is one of the biggest upsets in modern-day Test cricket! Who would have given them a chance especially after they were bowled out for 54 and lost by an innings against CA XI last week at this very venue? But they have not only silenced the cricketing pundits with this performance but have literally blown them away. They have developed a tough character and an ideal mix for a variety of conditions. Australia is one of the toughest countries to tour in red-ball cricket. This is not just a convincing win for Bangladesh, it’s a statement to all other nations that they can be a force to reckon with even in away conditions.

Coming back to the game, Cummins won the toss and chose to bat but it backfired on the hosts. Led by the young Hasan Mahmud who was highly impressive and recorded his career-best figures (6/55), the other seamers also chipped in to take all ten wickets to shot Australia out for 198. Tanzid laid the platform for them with a superb maiden Test ton while vital contributions from Mominul, Shanto and Mehidy ensured that the visitors took a massive 228-run lead.

The ball was in their court and they capitalised. Hasan Mahmud was once again incisive and finished with 9 wickets in the game while it was Mehidy who gave it a rip and weaved his magic (5/66) to run through the Australian middle and lower order. Green stood tall amongst the ruins as he raised a maiden Test ton on home soil but it wasn’t nearly enough as the others left a lot to be desired. Bangladesh needed just 57 to win. Tanzid departed for a duck but the duo of Shadman and Mominul were clinical and ensured that there were no further hiccups as they took their team to the finish line with consummate ease. Special mention to the Bangladeshi batters - they had to tackle the elite trio of Starc, Hazlewood and Cummins and they did that with utmost conviction.
This is Bangladesh’s first Test win in Australia in three matches. It is also just their second win over Australia in seven Tests, after the 2017 Mirpur triumph.
This is Bangladesh’s second Test win in SENA countries after their famous victory in Mount Maunganui in 2022.
Australia have lost a home Test to an Asian team other than India for the first time in 31 years, since 1995.
Bangladesh’s 9-wicket win is their second-biggest Test victory by wickets, behind their 10-wicket win over Pakistan in Rawalpindi in 2024.

Bangladesh is the quickest Asian team to register its first Test win on Australian soil, doing so in just 3 Tests, ahead of Pakistan (7) and India (12), while Sri Lanka remains winless after 15 attempts.

What a fantastic victory, forever etched into the folklore of Bangladesh cricket! Bangladeshi fans across the globe will be over the moon celebrating this historic milestone. Their pace bowling attack has improved drastically over the years, and even without their strike weapon Nahid Rana, they have done brilliantly to dismantle a formidable Australian lineup in their own backyard. This win has boosted their chances in the World Championship table. Bangladesh gained 12 crucial away points, boosting their PCT (points percentage) to 66.67% to solidify 4th place and put them within reach of the top three. Meanwhile, Australia's loss of 12 home points caused their top-spot PCT (points percentage) to drop to 77.78%, shrinking their safety margin ahead of a demanding Test schedule ahead, which includes 5 away Tests against India.
